paper_id: Assignment problem in requirements driven agent collaboration and its implementation
title: Assignment Problem in Requirements Driven Agent Collaboration and its Implementation
venue: 9th Int. Conf. on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (AAMAS 2010)
motivation: SOA ignores autonomy of service providers and consumers; providers cannot participate in discovery/composition.
problem_framing: NP-complete task allocation among self-interested agents with reservation payoff constraints in decentralized setting.
key_insight: Bridging assignment problem with normative systems via Kripke structure enables leveraging existing game/mechanism theory.
method_signature: Negotiation-based task allocation modeled as Kripke structure with CTL-expressed normative constraints.
evaluation_criteria: Maximizing total satisfaction degree (service + request agents) while satisfying reservation payoff thresholds.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: 96% success rate but 4/100 failed; agents with higher proportion often break negotiation quickly.
evidence_for_taste: the autonomy of the two parties has been ignored
agents may not want to disclose their reservation payoff
not an agent which can satisfy the request agent by its own
65 of them have the value larger than 0.9
thinking_moves: 从NP-complete证明反向建立理论框架，通过Kripke结构将组合优化问题连接到规范系统领域
先展示形式化复杂性(n=2特殊情况的归约证明)，再提出可扩展的谈判机制作为启发式解
用CTL逻辑表达每个agent的目标，将系统目标转化为合取式，实现规范系统的可组合性
将隐私约束作为方法论障碍显式承认，而非绕过它
extraction_notes: All core signals extracted from paper content. Authors cite prior RDAC work [17][16] but this is not self-citation for current paper's core contribution.
